title: Glutamine Flux Imaging Using Genetically Encoded Sensors
protocol: Seed cos7 cells at ~70-80% confluency in Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle Medium (DMEM) + 10% cosmic calf serum and 100 U/ml penicillin/streptomycin, either on sterile 25 mm glass coverslips placed in the 6-well culture dish or 8-well glass-bottom slides.
Incubate at 37 °C, 5% CO2, 100% humidity for 24 hr.
Exchange the growth medium to DMEM +10% cosmic calf serum (no antibiotics).
Grow O/N at 37 °C, 5% CO2 at 100% humidity.
Add 0.4 mg each of plasmid DNA encoding the glutamine sensor and mCherry-tagged ASCT2 to 50 ml serum-free media (OPTI-MEM) and mix gently.
Add 1 ml of transfection reagent to 50 ml serum-free media.
Incubate at RT for 5 min.
Mix the two solutions containing DNA and transfection reagent.
Incubate the mixture for 20 min.
Gently add the transfection reagent on top of the cells and mix gently by rocking the chamber.
Incubate for 24 hr at 37 °C, 5% CO2, 100% humidity.
Exchange the medium to DMEM + 10% Cosmic Calf Serum (CCS) + 100 unit of penicillin/streptomycin after 24 hr.
Prepare perfusion buffer A-F.
Attach stopcocks to 50 ml syringes, close the stopcocks then fill them with the perfusion solutions.
Open the stopcock for a brief period to fill the head space in the stopcock with the buffer.
Switch on the 8-channel, gravity-feed perfusion system with a perfusion pencil.
Select “Manual Mode” under Select Function option.
Place a waste container under the perfusion pencil.
Manually activate the ports by pressing the corresponding numbers.
Fill the tubings using a 10 ml syringe containing water.
Close the port after filling with water.
Set the syringes containing buffers A-F on the perfusion system ports 1-6.
Open the stopcocks to start the flow of buffers, maintaining a flow rate around 0.8 ml/min.
Press cancel once on the perfusion controller to return to the “Select Function” menu.
Toggle to “Edit Program” option and type in the perfusion protocol indicated in Table 1.
Save the perfusion program.
Take the cells out of the incubator.
Wash the cells twice with the perfusion buffer.
Set the cells on the stage for observation.
Connect the perfusion system to the chamber.
If an open chamber is used, set up another pump to remove perfusion solution from the chamber.
Open Slidebook software.
Start a new slide.
Mount the slide onto the fluorescent microscope stage.
Find the cells co-expressing the sensor and ASCT-mCherry using appropriate filter sets under “FOCUS” function.
Adjust gain by clicking “Camera” tab and sliding the slider under “gain”.
Adjust the neutral density filter setting from the neutral density filter drop-down menu.
Acquire images of cells with donor (mTFP1)exdonor(mTFP1)em, donor(mTFP1)exacceptor(venus)em, and acceptor(mTFP1)exacceptor(venus)em channels.
Click “Image Capture” in the acquisition window.
Specify the filters that are going to be used.
Adjust the exposure time by clicking the “TEST” button and typing the desired exposure time next to the filter settings.
Ensure all three channels are exposed for the same length.
Take the expected FRET efficiency change and fold increase into account when adjusting imaging parameters.
Draw a region of interest using the regions tool in the software.
Alternatively, select pixels above certain intensity and convert them into regions.
Click Mask – Segment, then move the sliding bar to highlight desired areas.
Select “time lapse” in the capture type box.
Specify the interval (10 seconds) and time points for the experiment.
Draw a region in an area without any fluorescent cells for background subtraction.
Right-click the region drawn, then set it as a background.
Select the desired program under “Select Function - Run programs.”
Toggle to the saved program and hit ENTER on the perfusion controller.
Ensure perfusion and imaging experiment start at the same time by clicking “Start” in the capture window simultaneously with pressing a key on the perfusion controller.
Perform the same perfusion protocol using cells expressing a sensor that is expected to be either saturated or unbound under the experimental condition.
Use FLIPQTV3.0_1.5μ as a control, which is saturated under the experimental condition.
Examine if sample drift has occurred during the experiment.
Draw Regions Of Interest (ROI)s on the image taken at timepoint 0.
Move the sliding bar to check if cells fall out of the ROIs in images taken later.
Use the tracking function to correct for drift by creating masks around the cells.
Select Mask – Segment to highlight regions containing cells.
Click Mask – Particle tracking – Basic particle tracking to track the regions.
Re-draw the ROIs and background region when necessary.
Export the mean intensity of the ROIs over the course of the experiment.
Click Statistics – Export – Ratio/timelapse data.
Plot the time course of the intensity ratio (DonorexAcceptorem / DonorexDonorem) as a proxy for substrate dynamics.
Calculate the maximal and minimal ratio change, Δrmax - Δrmin, using non-linear regression with the equation: Δr = [S]/(Kd+[S]) x (Δrmax - Δrmin) + Δrmin.
Determine the saturation (S) of the sensor at a given Δr using the equation: S = (Δr - Δrmin) / (Δrmax - Δrmin).
Convert the saturation into substrate concentration [S] using the equation: S = [S]/(Kd+[S]).
Plot the intensities of donor and acceptor over time to examine baseline drift due to photo-bleaching.
Perform a baseline correction by identifying appropriate timepoints according to perfusion system delay and cell transport activity.
Calculate a polynomial fitting that best describes the baseline.
Normalize raw intensity from each timepoint to the baseline.
Calculate the intensity ratio (DonorAcceptor / DonorDonor) from the normalized donor and acceptor intensities.
